title: Coordinates of a combination of coordinate wedges: the J-coordinate of Σ_I c_I·dx^I is c_J (dx^I(e_J) = δ_IJ)
statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ. Write ℝ^P = Eucl P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) and b_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 (i ∈ Fin P) for the standard basis. Let SimonMultiIndex k P = Fin k ↪o Fin P be the finite type of strictly increasing multi-indices (order embeddings). For I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P let dx^I := wedgeCovectors k (fun j ↦ EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)) ∈ Covector (Eucl P) k be the coordinate k-covector dx^{I(0)} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^{I(k−1)}, where EuclideanSpace.proj i is the i-th coordinate functional. For a k-covector γ and J ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P let euclideanCovectorCoordinate γ J := γ(b_{J(0)}, …, b_{J(k−1)}). Then for every family of real coefficients c : SimonMultiIndex k P → ℝ and every J ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P, euclideanCovectorCoordinate (Σ_{I ∈ SimonMultiIndex k P} c_I · dx^I) J = c_J. In particular dx^I(b_{J(0)}, …, b_{J(k−1)}) = δ_{IJ}.
lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (c : SimonMultiIndex k P → ℝ) (J : SimonMultiIndex k P), euclideanCovectorCoordinate (∑ I : SimonMultiIndex k P, c I • wedgeCovectors k (fun j => EuclideanSpace.proj (I j)) : Covector (Eucl P) k) J = c J
